correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 the exact page/hub update gives a four-interval parity-dependent quotient. Every possible initial triple (a,b,s) is covered, and for each such triple the page word either remains unchanged in a tie or becomes homogeneous. Exhaustive cases prove immediate-period populations, transient-to-period-two tails, transient-to-fixed counts, and entry at most two. Subtracting known disjoint counts from 2^(n+2) gives the remaining E_{1,2}; all formulas are nonnegative at n=2. Uniform asymptotics use central-binomial estimate. The direct simulator verifies 131056 labelled states for n=2..14; independent binomial-weighted quotient verifies n=2..120. Neither finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full first-entry distribution is a natural dynamical invariant measuring basins, not only recurrent states. On the canonical triangular-book family it sharpens general convergence to an exact at-most-two clock, gives five nontrivial binomial populations, and separates an immediate-period parity dichotomy (exponential vs n^(-1/2)) from a common asymptotic one-quarter eventual basin. This distinction is not inferable from recurrent-state counts and has a clear mathematical motivation in agreement dynamics with tie-memory leaves.
